description:
Mountain Mahogany (Cercocarpus spp.) is a shrub or small tree that is highly dangerous to cats. The main risk comes from its leaves and seeds, which contain compounds called cyanogenic glycosides (such as prunasin).

When a cat chews or crushes the leaves, these compounds break down and release toxic cyanide gas into the body. This poison stops the body's cells from using oxygen. Wilted or dried leaves are even more dangerous than fresh ones, as the poison is released more easily. If a cat swallows a seed whole without chewing, the poison might not be released, but chewing it is a serious hazard.

Signs of poisoning can happen very fast. A cat may breathe rapidly or gasp for air, have unusually bright red gums, drool heavily, or show wide pupils. In severe cases, it can cause seizures or loss of consciousness. If you suspect your cat ate any part of this plant, please immediately contact a veterinarian or emergency animal hospital, as this is a life-threatening emergency.
name: Mountain Mahogany
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: prunasin (cyanogenic glycoside); wilted leaves most dangerous
Mechanism: prunasin releases HCN via beta-glucosidase, inhibiting cytochrome c oxidase and halting cellular respiration
Symptoms: rapid breathing, weakness, dilated pupils, drooling; severe cases cause seizures, coma, and respiratory failure
Wilted or fallen leaves pose a higher risk than fresh leaves due to accelerated cyanogenic conversion
Seek veterinary care immediately if ingestion is suspected — cyanide toxicity can progress within minutes

symptoms.name: Respiratory distress (panting, gasping for breath, or labored breathing)
Unusually red or pink gums (bright red mucous membranes)
Shock, seizures (convulsions), loss of consciousness, and coma
